news.title: UEFA warns FIFA of legal action over failed World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: European football body UEFA has threatened FIFA with legal action over Gianni Infantino’s failed plan to sell a stake in future World Cup profits to private investors, and said any potential evidence should not be destroyed. Infantino’s secretive proposal to raise US$4.2 billion (NZ$7.1 billion) from investors including the New York investment firm of Joshua Kushner was dropped Saturday, days after the revelation in media reports provoked a global furore. UEFA led the backlash, and on Friday its 55 member federations met to agree to boycott all FIFA events and competitions while the proposal was active. Now lawyers for UEFA have informed FIFA that the European body is “actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints ... arising out of and in connection with the FFE (FIFA Forward Enterprise) plan proposed by FIFA and all related matters”.

news.title: FIFA scrap World Cup sell-off plan after backlash
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA “will not proceed” with plans to sell stakes in a company which would run the commercial and operational aspects of its competitions, a statement from president Gianni Infantino said. The plan, which would include the men’s and women’s World Cups, has been rejected by three continental confederations with UEFA insisting its nations would boycott FIFA events.

news.title: Harry Kane planning on talks for contract extension, taking run at 2030 World Cup
news.lede: According to a report from Sport Bild’s Christian Falk, Bayern Munich star Harry Kane is inching closer to resuming contract talks with the Bavarians. That is news that will be welcomed by many fans, but Kane also wants to continue onward in Bavaria to potentially take a run at playing for England at the 2030 World Cup: > There was a former Tottenham manager who once claimed that Harry Kane has an idea of coming back to England to compete for Alan Shearer’s goal record in the Premier League. I can concretely say that this is not true. He’s not so keen on the goal record and would prefer to get titles with Bayern Munich.

news.title: UEFA declare loss of confidence in Infantino after World Cup sell-off controversy
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA president Gianni Infantino has “lost the confidence” of UEFA over a plan to sell stakes in a World Cup company to private investors, the European football governing body has said. Infantino announced overnight that the plan would not proceed after three confederations rejected it, with UEFA going further and saying it would boycott FIFA competitions until the proposal was scrapped.
